# 2 Baruch Chapter 41 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**41:1** And-I-answered and-said: For-whom and-for-how-many will-these-things-be? Or-who-will-be-worthy-to-live in-that-time?

**41:2** I-will-speak before-you everything-that-I-think, and-I-will-ask-of-you concerning [all]-the-things which-concern-me.

**41:3** For-I-know-well that-many-who-have-sinned-once are-[now]-righteous and-many-who-have-[lived]-righteously but-who-have-transgressed afterward — [some of them] are-in-their-transgression.

**41:4** And-on-account-of-this it-is-necessary to-weigh-the-deeds-of-a-man in-a-balance at-the-end.

**41:5** For-who-can-say: I-have-sinned and-have-not-transgressed; and-who-will-say I-have-not-done-evil?

**41:6** For-those-who-are-wicked — they-will-receive-according-to-their-wickedness; and-those-who-are-righteous — they-will-receive according-to-their-righteousness. And-they-who-are-mixed [shall-be determined] by-whether-good-is-found [to-outweigh].

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Chapter 41 introduces the question of "mixed" people — those who are neither clearly righteous nor clearly wicked. This is 2 Baruch's most nuanced soteriological discussion, anticipating a weighing of deeds. The balance/scale metaphor (v.4) is drawn from Egyptian and Mesopotamian traditions.*
